findings.title: Unknown or unavailable provider configuration can silently become manual card checkout
findings.risk: A configured managed payment can be recorded as a plain card sale without sending a payment to Dojo. The native fault test stopped before confirmation; the actual production commit branch was exercised only with isolated spies.

source.detail: Provider selection requires enabled and ready; all other cases become null.
Completion guard has no provider-loading, unreadable-config or enabled-not-ready barrier.
Startup uses Promise.allSettled without retaining rejected provider-read state.
Dojo-unavailable case is classified as ordinary card rather than blocked.
No selected managed provider means ordinary commitSale, without a Dojo request.
Customer accounts already distinguish unavailable providers and block read failures.

nativeEvidence.reportedBy: Root agent controlling current isolated native QA app
nativeEvidence.persistentFault: Only the public QA Dojo configuration was temporarily replaced with malformed JSON after the exact original file was recoverably moved. A cold WebView reload changed payment from Dojo to Card; selecting Card exposed enabled Confirm Card Payment and manual approval instructions for the preserved £11 trolley. No financial confirmation was clicked. Original config restored by moving back the preserved file; valid enabled dedicated QA configuration and controls restored; secret files untouched.
nativeEvidence.oneShotFault: The provider.dojo.read one-shot checkpoint was armed, entered and rejected. A later successful configuration read self-repaired the store and the Dojo label remained; this single-fault case alone did not reproduce the persistent fail-open UI.

findings.recommendation: Keep explicit loading/error states and fail closed until current provider settings are known. Block enabled-not-ready configurations. Preserve manual card only when both successfully loaded provider configurations are intentionally disabled, and use clear external-approval confirmation.

findings.title: Overlapping recovery can omit the requested provider and return another provider's result

source.detail: Every overlapping caller receives the current promise even if it requested a different provider.
Startup requests SumUp and Dojo recovery concurrently.
The unfiltered periodic recovery is a mitigation, running again every 60 seconds.

findings.risk: Dojo work can be delayed while the UI reports a SumUp-only result. The periodic all-provider recovery mitigates permanent stranding; this is not a demonstrated lost payment.
findings.recommendation: Make overlapping calls drain the union of requested providers or use a single all-provider sweep. Only report results for providers actually inspected.

findings.title: Older operator guidance disagrees with current sandbox timeout behavior

source.detail: Expired-payment section describes automatic sandbox cleanup as removed.
Current checkout supplies the guarded sandbox timeout-cleanup callback.
Current account collection supplies the same guarded callback.
Sandbox Expired plus Created can invoke cleanup and requires fresh provider finality.

findings.risk: Operators or UAT reviewers may expect only the receipt-review path, while sandbox checkout can automatically attempt verified cleanup. Live/Unknown keys remain excluded from that automatic branch.
findings.recommendation: After deciding the intended policy, update the current operator/UAT instructions and clearly distinguish sandbox cleanup, live receipt review and historical tests.
